Use FastAPI's **lifespan events** to run setup code once, before the app starts handling requests. You can define logic (code) that should be executed before the application **starts up**. This means that this code will be executed **once**, **before** the application **starts receiving requests**.[1] The docs describe this exact use case: load the model before the requests are handled, but only right before the application starts receiving requests, not while the code is being loaded.[1]

**Why not load it at module level?** That would also mean that it would load the model even if you are just running a simple automated test, then that test would be slow because it would have to wait for the model to load[1].

You can also run cleanup code at shutdown. You can define logic (code) that should be executed when the application is shutting down. In this case, this code will be executed once, after having handled possibly many requests.[1]

**Example:** The SQL databases tutorial uses a startup event to create the database tables when the application starts[4]:

```python
app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event("startup")
def on_startup():
    create_db_and_tables()
```

You could follow the same pattern by loading your model inside the startup function instead.

The excerpt I have from the Lifespan Events page ends before it shows the recommended `lifespan` implementation. For the full code, see the rest of that page: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/events/
